problems.note: The answer 3.5 is decimal notation, which Grade 2 children don't use. The narration should say 'three and a half' so it can be understood by ear. The number line also needs its half-step marks announced, because a child who can't see the line can't tell where 3 and a half is.

7 groups of 6 (7 addends of 6) is a multiplication-fact load closer to Grade 3 than the Grade 2 repeated-adding skill. 'Half carton' is also unclear by ear, since a child may not know a carton holds 12 eggs. Consider a simpler item such as 'bags of 5' or fewer groups.

'Move the frog to where it lands' depends on seeing the 0 to 10 line. The narration should read out the line's endpoints and step so the item can be played from sound alone. The same applies to the other number-line items.
